item.title: Safe and Trustworthy Autonomous Systems in Real-World Environments
item.content:encoded:
Heye Huang, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST)

Inhi Kim, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST)

Boqi Li, Beihang University

Haotian Shi, Tongji University

Lei Yang, Nanyang Technological University

Kailai Sun, Massachusetts Institute of Technology

Autonomous systems operating in complex real-world environments face significant challenges in ensuring safety, reliability, and generalization. This special issue seeks research that advances trustworthy autonomy through integration of data-driven learning with structured knowledge, world models, formal verification, and uncertainty reasoning. Contributions should address both average-case and long-tail safety-critical scenarios, with emphasis on how autonomous systems can identify risks, adapt continually, and coordinate with other agents.

The scope includes autonomous vehicles, robotics, embodied AI, and other safety-critical platforms. Submissions may combine learning, optimization, control, simulation, and human-centered methods provided they clearly contribute to trustworthy autonomous behavior. The issue welcomes original research, reviews, benchmarks, and perspective articles demonstrating methodological novelty, rigorous evaluation, or insights transferable to real-world autonomous system deployment.

Appel publié par Expert Systems. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

  • Risk representation and uncertainty-aware perception
  • Behavior prediction and occupancy modeling
  • Scene modeling and world models

  • Continual learning and self-evolving autonomy

  • Digital twins and safety assessment
  • Connected and automated vehicles
  • V2X-enabled cooperation
  • Multi-agent coordination
  • Traffic-level autonomy and infrastructure intelligence
  • System-wide mobility optimization

item.title: Governing safety in connected and automated vehicles: evidence, ethics, and policy innovations
item.content:encoded:
This special issue focuses on governance frameworks and policy approaches for ensuring safety in connected and automated vehicles. The issue seeks to integrate empirical evidence, ethical considerations, and innovative policy solutions to address the complex challenges posed by autonomous vehicle deployment in real-world transportation systems.

item.title: Mathematical Foundations for Trustworthy AI Applications in Transportation Systems
item.content:encoded:
This special issue focuses on the mathematical and computational foundations necessary for developing trustworthy artificial intelligence applications in transportation systems. As AI increasingly influences critical transportation decisions affecting safety, efficiency, and equity, there is an urgent need for rigorous mathematical frameworks that ensure these systems are reliable, interpretable, and accountable.

The special issue welcomes contributions that advance the theoretical understanding and practical implementation of trustworthy AI in transportation. This includes work on mathematical models that enhance transparency, ensure robustness against adversarial attacks, quantify uncertainties, and address fairness concerns in transportation algorithms and systems.

Submissions should demonstrate how mathematical and computational approaches contribute to building trustworthy AI systems that stakeholders can understand, verify, and depend upon for critical transportation applications.

Appel publié par Transportation Research Part B Methodological. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Mathematical frameworks for explainability and interpretability in transportation AI
  • Formal verification and validation methods for autonomous vehicles
  • Trustworthy machine learning algorithms for traffic prediction and management
  • Robustness and adversarial resilience in transportation systems
  • Uncertainty quantification in AI-based transportation applications
  • Fairness and bias mitigation in transportation decision-making systems
  • Privacy-preserving techniques in transportation data analytics
  • Game-theoretic approaches to multi-agent transportation systems
  • Causal inference methods for transportation research
  • Probabilistic and Bayesian methods in transportation AI

Timeline

  • December 1, 2026: Full paper submission deadline
